Altogether forty types of tableware were created. The fact
that almost all pottery from Late Roman to Umayyad
times is of local production underlines once more
Jerash’s quality as an almost industrial pottery producer
over centuries. It is interesting though that the expected
standardization of types at a large-scale production cen-
tre like Jerash does not exist. This becomes particularly
clear in the case of the Jerash Bowls. We do not see this
phenomenon in general at other large-scale production
sites, neither in ancient nor in modern times.19

Juglet, Amphoriskos, Pilgrim Flask

The variety of small juglets, amphoriskoi, and other small
vessels is high;568 the quantity compared to the other cat-
egories very low (Fig. 2.69).569 Every single fragment is a
unique find. Therefore, dividing them by their morpho­
logical appearance does not make any sense, since there
are only a few samples per group. The first small juglets
occur in Late Roman/Early Byzantine context.570 Most
of the finds, however, were found in Late Byzantine/
Early Umayyad context.571 Of Late Byzantine date are
also two pilgrim flasks. A single small flask was found in
the earthquake destruction layer of Umayyad house K. It
is the latest find of this set of small vessels. The produc-
tion is probably local as they are all made in the typical
Jerash manner. The early forms show a thin reddish slip
on the inside and outside of the vessel, others occur in
grey ware.

 1. Medium Iron/Low Lime: Fe2O3 = c. 4–6 per cent;

    apart from when Fe2O3 > 8 per cent; abs. CaO =
   1–5 per cent.

    Fe2O3: CaO ratio 0.5–2.5;
     abs. CaO = 3–11 per cent.
 4. High Lime: CaO > 11 per cent.

Admittedly, these pXRF compositional groups are an
abstraction: although there are compositional and min-                                                                            Figure A2. Scatterplot comparing iron oxide and lime (pXRF).

boundaries. An example is the division of Group 3 and

ICP-MS (J14-Je-77-1030)7 seems to touch or overlap

oversimplification represented by the pXRF dataset and

All volumes in this series are evaluated by an Editorial Board, strictly on academic grounds,
based on reports prepared by referees who have been commissioned by virtue of their specialism
in the appropriate field. The Board ensures that the screening is done independently and with-
out conflicts of interest. The definitive texts supplied by authors are also subject to review by
the Board before being approved for publication. Further, the volumes are copyedited to con-
form to the publisher’s stylebook and to the best international academic standards in the field.
